predecessors.name: Chola Empire
predecessors.text: the Pandya country round Madurai: 'the Cholas had lost most of their control of the territories south of the river Kaveri' as Pandya power rose (Rajaraja III page)

successors.name: Tughlaq dynasty
successors.text: the Pandya country, which Ulugh Khan 'annexed ... as the Ma'bar province'

rulers.name: Sundara Pandya IV and Vira Pandya IV

ledger.x: 1216: Maravarman Sundara Pandyan I succeeds and the Pandyas rise over the Cholas.
1216 (year bridged): the Pandyas invade the Chola country.
1216 (year bridged): the Chola king submits.
1217 (year bridged): Mahendramangalam.
1217 (year bridged): the Chola overlordship ends with the restoration of Rajaraja III at Mahendramangalam.
1220: Tirunelveli and the Kerala coast join the Madurai country.
ledger.cp: unnamed rulers of the Pandya south and the Kerala coast

ledger.x: About 1220: the Pandyas pay tribute to the Hoysala king.
1236: Kongu and Palakkad.
1241: the Kaveri delta and the north of the Kongu plateau.
About 1245: the Hoysala hegemony over the Pandyas ends.
1258: Kanchipuram.
1258: Nellore.
c. 1258-1260: the last Cholas pay tribute. 'He subdued Chola Rajendra II c. 1258-1260 and made him pay tribute'; the Jatavarman page: Rajendra III accepted 'Pandyan overlordship' (no year).
1258: Jaffna becomes a Pandya feudatory.
By 1262: Kannanur.
By 1271 (bridge): Nellore leaves Pandya hands.
c. 1279: the Cholas end. 'A combined force of Hoysala Ramanatha and Chola Rajendra III was defeated by him c. 1279' (Kulasekara); the chola-empire dossier ends the dynasty then.
1284: the Pandyas take the Tooth Relic.

c. 1295 (year bridged): Veera Ballala III recovers the Tamil holdings. 'Pandyan rule over the Hoysala-held region lasted until Veera Ballala III recaptured it near the end of the 13th century'; the hoysala-kingdom dossier places it c. 1295.

c. 1309: Pandya control of Sri Lanka ends. 'Pandya control of Sri Lanka lasted until c. 1308-1309.' [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: the counterpart 'ceylon' is now the merged Sinhalese state (kingdom-of-dambadeniya was merged into ceylon, which starts in 1220); the pair 1284-1309 is the one occupation, so no split…
March 1311: Malik Kafur's army enters the Pandya country.
Late April 1311: the Khaljis return to Delhi with plunder.
1312: south Kerala is lost.
ledger.cp: rulers of south Kerala (not named by the page)

ledger.x: c. 1317: the Kakatiyas occupy Kanchi. 'After Alauddin's death in 1316, the Hoysala king Ballala launched a fresh invasion of the Pandya territory'; the Kakatiya commander Peda Rudra defeated Ballala, 'After this victory, he occupied Kanchi in the Pandya territory'; Devarinayaka 'defeated Vira Pandya' and the Kakatiyas…
1323: the Jaffna kingdom is independent.
1323: the Tughlaq army comes south.
1323 (bridge): the Kanchi occupation ends with the Kakatiya kingdom.
By 1325: the conquest is complete.
By 1325: the Pandya Empire becomes the Ma'bar province.

wars.name: Pandya-Chola-Hoysala war of 1216-1217
wars.outcome: The Pandyas sack Uraiyur and Thanjavur; Kulothunga III accepts Pandya overlordship; Rajaraja III, backed by the Hoysala Narasimha II, defeats them at Mahendramangalam on the Kaveri and is restored.

wars.name: Pandyan conquest of the Chola north and Nellore
wars.outcome: Kanchipuram taken and the Nellore Choda ruler killed in 1258; Rajendra III pays tribute c.

wars.name: Pandya-Hoysala war over Kannanur
wars.outcome: The Pandyas take Kannanur; Someshwara's counteroffensive of 1262 fails and he is killed; Ramanatha recovers Kannanur later.

wars.name: Pandya invasions of Sri Lanka
wars.outcome: Intervention of 1258, Veera Pandyan's of 1262-1264 and again 1270 (Jatavarman page); Tooth Relic taken in 1284; Pandya control to c.

wars.name: Pandya succession war and the Khalji invasion
wars.outcome: Sundara Pandya IV defeats his brother Vira Pandya IV; Malik Kafur raids the country in March-April 1311; Sundara regains South Arcot with Khalji help by 1314; Ballala III, who invaded the Pandya country, retreats to his capital.

wars.name: Tughlaq conquest of the Pandya country
wars.outcome: Expeditions of 1314 (Khusro Khan) and 1323 (Jauna Khan); the Pandya lands become the Ma'bar province before 1325.

certainty.note: No Pandya frontier is on the pages; the shapes are Cliopatria's.
